page: Google Cloud Platform x5-1376-32t-metal is an ultra-high-density bare-metal compute offering in the Memory Optimized server family. The machine delivers 1376 dedicated physical x86_64 cores alongside 32,768 GB of system memory. This architecture provides an extreme memory density of approximately 23.81 GB of RAM per dedicated core, catering specifically to monolithic workloads that cannot be distributed easily across clustered nodes.

Hardware provisions reflect pure bare-metal design principles. The configuration contains zero integrated GPUs and provides no local storage devices, requiring all persistent storage, scratch directories, and operating systems to be connected through external network-attached block infrastructure. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated, requiring private VPC configuration or dedicated external IP routing for public connectivity.

From an economic and operational perspective, allocating a bare-metal instance of this scale represents a qualitative commitment to monolithic memory infrastructure over horizontally scaled clusters. By consolidating extreme memory footprints into a single host, it eliminates the operational overhead and network latency bottlenecks associated with multi-node clustering, though it requires sufficient memory-bound application scale to justify the density. It is specifically fit for massive in-memory databases, ultra-large enterprise ERP platforms such as SAP HANA, real-time analytics engines, and high-core parallel in-memory simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform x5-1376-32t-metal is a bare-metal server in the Memory Optimized family designed for extreme-scale memory workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 1376 dedicated vCPUs and 32,768 GB of system memory, resulting in roughly 23.81 GB of RAM per core. The server includes zero discrete GPUs and features no onboard local storage, depending entirely on network-attached storage architectures for persistence. With zero included public IPv4 addresses, connectivity relies on cloud networking infrastructure. This hardware configuration is built to serve monolithic workloads requiring vast continuous memory spaces, such as enterprise in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive real-time analytical caches, and large parallel simulation engines that demand consolidation onto a single physical server.
